ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the graphs of the linear functions ${y}_{1}=kx$ and ${y}_{2}=-x+b$ intersect at point $A(1, 2)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $kx>-x+b$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the graph of linear functions $y_{1}=kx$ and $y_{2}=-x+b$ intersects at point $A(1,2)$,\\
it follows from the graph that the solution set of the inequality $kx>-x+b$ with respect to $x$ is $x>1$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{x>1}$.
